browserChecks: Published package serves the real React application and static assets
Browser registration creates a private workspace and authenticated session
Session credentials are absent from local storage, session storage and cookies
Customer creation persists through the browser form
Stale edit is rejected, the draft survives, and explicit reload allows a reviewed edit
A response lost after commit retries the same operation and creates exactly one customer
Deletion requires confirmation and removes an unused record
Plan and coupon forms persist typed pricing and discount contracts
Related record selectors create a subscription and correctly timed usage
Billing creates the expected USD 25 subtotal, USD 5 discount and USD 20 invoice
Payment controls preserve a decline, succeed a new attempt, and simulate the durable outbox
Server pagination and search agree on counts and reset the page offset
Viewer sign-in renders read-only controls and hides owner membership actions
Desktop and narrow layouts render without horizontal overflow
No uncaught browser JavaScript errors occurred
packaging: Published browser assets exactly match the final Vite build
Published package contains no application database or App_Data files
Backend, test and frontend dependency lock files exist
dependencyAudits: npm full installed tree and NuGet API transitive tree reported no known advisories at verification time.

observations: Desktop navigation, metrics, simulator controls and paginated record rows are aligned and readable.
Narrow layout stacks metrics and controls, wraps navigation into three columns and keeps record actions visible without horizontal overflow.
Visible text is correctly encoded; status and action labels are legible with no overlapping controls.
Screenshots show fictional data from the final passing packaged-browser run.

limitations: Loopback-only single-node SQLite simulator; no public deployment, real payment provider, outgoing HTTP delivery or automatic billing scheduler.
USD/EUR/GBP only; no taxes, proration, refunds, credit notes or currency conversion.
Relational identity/relationship tables wrap immutable JSON records; some internal workflows materialize bounded collections. Limit: 5,000 domain records per workspace.
Eight-hour in-memory browser session, 24-hour durable operation receipts; pending browser retry state is lost when the tab closes. Auth registration/login are outside the receipt protocol.
Owner/Operator/Viewer membership management is implemented, but no password-change/recovery flow, invitation email, federated identity, existing-account workspace linking or owner transfer.
Original data was not opened or replaced. Unknown database files are refused; migration requires separate reviewed work or a new learning database path.
Provider callback signatures use a custom local HMAC protocol, not Stripe compatibility. Audit and provider-event history have no retention UI.
Historical documentation is labeled and preserved; proposed course exercises are not counted as implemented functionality.
